answer: Each agent identity must lock a nontransferable bond before it can trade, then earn reputation through randomly selected tasks such as timber, quill, and opal orders. Other agents can challenge its signed work; a failed challenge slashes the bond and removes its accumulated reputation. Because the minimum bond is required per identity and reputation cannot be copied, a Sybil attacker must finance every fake agent and patiently rebuild its history, making mass identity creation costly.
